Text: Taking omeprazole long-term may cause you to develop stomach growths called fundic gland polyps.
Talk with your doctor about this risk.
If you use this medicine for longer than 3 years, you could develop a vitamin B-12 deficiency.
Talk to your doctor if you develop symptoms.
These symptoms include shortness of breath, lightheadedness, irregular heartbeat, muscle weakness, pale skin, feeling tired, mood changes, and tingling or numbness in the arms and legs.
Common side effects of omeprazole may include:
cold symptoms such as stuffy nose, sneezing, sore throat (especially in children);
fever (especially in children);
stomach pain, gas;
nausea, vomiting, diarrhea; or
headache.
This is not a complete list of side effects and others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

The relation 'has long term risk' in the triplet is defined as 'Long-term use of the subject drug may lead to the health risk or condition specified by the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. B. 'related to': The subject drug is associated with the medical condition or disease specified by the object entity.
C. 'may be used for': The subject drug may be used for the purpose or condition specified by the object entity.
D. 'has warning': The subject drug carries a safety warning or precaution about the risk or situation specified by the object entity.
